title: Geometric-resource bounds and permutation-averaged success probabilities for the WZP algorithm
authors: Linlin Ye, Linmao Wang, Zhaoqi Wu, Shao-Ming Fei
abstract: Solving linear systems of equations is a fundamental task in machine learning and optimization. In this work, we extend the original WZP algorithm from real symmetric linear systems to complex Hermitian linear systems. We then study the success probability of the modified WZP algorithm from a resource-theoretic perspective. By expressing the postselection success probability as the expectation value of a positive operator, we derive upper and lower bounds of the maximal success probability over separable, incoherent, and real pure states. These bounds further establish connections between the maximal success probability and geometric entanglement, coherence, and imaginarity. We further show that, under permutation averaging, the averaged success probability is an affine function of the coherence fraction, with its dependence determined by the alignment between the success operator and the equal-superposition state. We also investigate the preprocessed WZP algorithm under subgroup-constrained preprocessing. For the two-level family, the optimal success probability is determined by the maximal projection weight onto the orbit of the target projector. Our results provide a unified perspective on the WZP success probability under different operational constraints.
summary: This paper rigorously analyzes the success probability of the WZP algorithm when applied to complex Hermitian linear systems. By using a resource-theoretic framework, the authors derive bounds connecting the maximal success probability to geometric measures like entanglement and coherence. This provides a unified, geometric perspective on the limitations and performance of quantum algorithms.
main_problem: The paper extends the analysis of the WZP algorithm success probability from real to complex Hermitian linear systems and derives resource-theoretic bounds on this probability.
main_result: It establishes connections between the maximal success probability and geometric entanglement, coherence, and imaginarity, and shows that the averaged success probability is an affine function of the coherence fraction.
method: The analysis uses resource-theoretic methods, expressing success probability as an expectation value of a positive operator, and employs geometric measures to derive upper and lower bounds.
model_or_system: The core model is solving complex Hermitian linear systems of equations, $A|\mathbf{x}angle = |\mathbf{b}angle$, where the success probability is analyzed using an idealized spectral success operator $M$.
key_observables: Success probability ($P_0$), Geometric coherence ($C_g$), Geometric entanglement ($E_g$), and Geometric imaginarity ($I_g$).
important_parameters: Coherence fraction, spectral eigenvalues ($\omega_1, \omega_2$), and the structure of the input state $|\mathbf{b}angle$ (e.g., separable, incoherent, or real pure states).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on expressing the success probability as an expectation value of a positive operator, and some results assume non-degenerate leading eigenvalues.
paper_structure: The paper reviews the WZP algorithm and geometric measures, modifies the algorithm for complex Hermitian systems, derives resource-theoretic bounds, studies permutation averaging, and investigates constrained preprocessing.
why_interesting: It provides a deep theoretical link between the performance of quantum algorithms (like solving linear systems) and fundamental geometric resource quantities (coherence, entanglement) in quantum information theory.
